lines.text: Do you know how incognito mode works? Most people think it makes them invisible. It doesn't.
When you close an incognito window, your browser forgets that session's history, cookies and form data. On your device, it never happened.
But the websites you visit still see you. And your internet provider, or your school or work network, can still see which sites you reach.
Every request carries your IP address. It can point to your provider, and often your city.
And the moment you log in to an account, that site knows exactly who you are. Incognito or not.
In twenty twenty four, Google settled a lawsuit over tracking in incognito mode, and agreed to delete billions of records.
So incognito protects you from the next person who uses your laptop. Not from the internet.
Orbi Transfer has an anonymous mode built for sharing. No account, a throwaway ID, and other users can't see your location, your name, or your device.
